# Weather

One program, two dialects. Below ~700px it is a phone app — a scrolling list
of cities, each of which expands in place into a full-page view. Above 700px
it is a desktop app — a sidebar of cities beside a grid of the same cards.
Nothing forks but layout and input: one card vocabulary, one set of drawn
instruments, one truth.

If this is your first Declare program, the shape to hold onto:

- **A program is one tree.** `App [ … ]` at the bottom of this file is the
  root; everything else here is a `class` — a reusable component — that the
  tree instantiates. `name = value` sets an attribute; `name: Type = value`
  declares a new one; `name: Type [ … ]` is a child component.
- **`{ }` is a relationship, not an assignment.** `width = { parent.width - 32 }`
  stays true forever: whenever anything it reads changes, it re-evaluates.
  There is no render loop to trigger and no subscription to manage — the
  whole app is such relationships, with a handful of handlers that assign
  plain values and let the relationships follow.
- **One truth.** `data` (in the App) holds the cities. The selected city is
  an index into it; every card, sky, and label derives from `app.city`, so
  switching cities is one number changing and the whole surface re-derives.
- **Motion is a value.** The row-to-page transition is a single scalar,
  `openT`, owned by a spring. Every travelling element positions itself with
  `lerp(rowSeat, pageSeat, openT)` — so the transition is interruptible and
  reversible by construction, because reversing is just the spring re-aiming.
- **Data displays are drawn.** The dials, bars, moon, and icons live in
  weather-art.declare as `draw()` components — code that re-runs when its
  inputs change, never per frame.

include [ "weather-art.declare" ]

script {
    // ── the numbers more than one place must agree on ──────────────────────
    // A `script { }` block is plain TypeScript; its top-level constants and
    // functions are readable from any `{ }` body in the file. Everything
    // that appears only once stays a literal where it is used.

    const SMALL_CARD_H = 176    // natural height of a one-slot card
    const CONDENSE_SPAN = 120   // scroll distance over which the hero condenses
    const EDGE_SLACK = 160      // how far past the viewport a sky reaches
    const LIST_TOP = 62         // where the phone list's rows begin (below search)
    const ROW_H = 92            // a list row at rest
    const ROW_GAP = 10          // the air between two rows
    const HERO_H = 268          // the opened row: name, temperature, condition
    const LIST_TAIL = 40        // breathing room after the last row
    const SIDEBAR_W = 340       // the desktop city list, and where the content starts

    // ── a debug arm for watching the transition ────────────────────────────
    // `?slow` runs every spring ten times slower; `?slow=N` picks the factor.
    // The MOTION is unchanged — only its clock is stretched — because the
    // damping ratio ζ = c / 2√(km) is what shapes a spring, and holding it
    // fixed while slowing by N means k/N² and c/N. The rest threshold scales
    // too (1/N): velocities are N times smaller at the end, so an unscaled
    // epsilon would call the arrival early and cut the tail off.

    const SLOW: number = (() => {
        if (typeof location == "undefined") return 1
        // the lookahead matters: without it `?slowland` matches this too, and
        // the spring silently runs ten times slower than the reader asked for
        const m = location.search.match(/[?&]slow(?:=(\d+))?(?![a-z])/)
        if (m == null) return 1
        return m[1] == null ? 10 : Math.max(1, Number(m[1]))
        })()

    function slowK(k: number): number { return k / (SLOW * SLOW) }
    function slowC(c: number): number { return c / SLOW }
    function slowEps(e: number): number { return e / SLOW }

    function fmtTemp(n: number): string { return "" + Math.round(n) + "°" }

    /** Read a value between two ends. Every travelling element in the city
     *  view is one of these — which is why a position and a font size can
     *  animate together without a keyframe anywhere. */
    function lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number { return a + (b - a) * t }

    /** 0 until `v` passes `start`, then rising at `speed` — an opacity that
     *  arrives partway through a transition. (Anything past 1 renders as 1.) */
    function fadeIn(v: number, start: number, speed: number): number {
        return Math.max(0, (v - start) * speed)
    }

    /** 1 at rest, falling at `speed` as `v` rises — an opacity that leaves
     *  early in a transition. */
    function fadeOut(v: number, speed: number): number {
        return Math.max(0, 1 - v * speed)
    }

    /** One instant, read at a place: `ms` is the shared clock, `tzMin` the
     *  place's offset from UTC in minutes. Wall-clock arithmetic only. */
    function localTime(ms: number, tzMin: number): string {
        if (ms <= 0) return ""
        const d = new Date(ms + tzMin * 60000)
        let h = d.getUTCHours()
        const m = d.getUTCMinutes()
        const ap = h < 12 ? "AM" : "PM"
        h = h % 12
        if (h == 0) h = 12
        return "" + h + ":" + (m < 10 ? "0" : "") + m + " " + ap
    }
    }


// ── the shared card chrome ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Every card is a frosted panel with a small uppercase caption. Subclasses
// add their content; instances set `label` (empty = no caption row).
//
// Note the two grid attributes a card DECLARES about itself: `span` (how many
// columns it occupies) and `baseH` (its natural height, when it is willing to
// be stretched to level the grid — see MasonryLayout in weather-art). The
// layout reads these; the card stays the authority on its own shape.

class Card extends View [ cornerRadius = 20, clip = true,
    span: number = 1,
    baseH: number = 0,
    grows: boolean = true,
    fill = #FFFFFF14, backdrop = { frost(14, 1.25) },
    stroke = { stroke(1, 0xFFFFFF29) },
    label: string = "",
    icon: string = "",

    // `classroot` reaches the root of the component being defined — here,
    // the Card itself — so a child can read the class's own attributes.

    cap: View [ x = 14, y = 12, height = 14, width = { parent.width - 28 },
        visible = { classroot.label != "" },
        capText: Text [ fontSize = 11.5, fontWeight = semibold, textColor = #FFFFFFA8,
            letterSpacing = 0.6, wrap = false, text = { classroot.label } ]
        ]
    ]


// ── the hourly strip ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// One column per hour: time, icon, temperature. `:name` is a DATAPATH read —
// this component is replicated over a list of records (see HourStrip below),
// and each copy reads fields from its own record.

class HourCol extends View [ width = 58, height = 92,
    timeText: Text [ x = center, y = 0, fontSize = 15, fontWeight = semibold, textColor = white,
        wrap = false, text = :t ],
    icon: WIcon [ x = center, y = 30, width = 30, height = 30, kind = { "" + :icon } ],

    // a zero temperature marks the sunrise/sunset entry, which shows a word
    // instead of a number — and a word does not fit a column sized for two
    // digits, so it takes the smaller size and sits on the same baseline

    tempText: Text [ x = center, fontSize = { :temp > 0 ? 20 : 14 },
        y = { :temp > 0 ? 68 : 72 },
        fontWeight = medium, textColor = white,
        wrap = false, text = { :temp > 0 ? fmtTemp(:temp) : (:icon == "sunrise" ? "Sunrise" : "Sunset") } ]
    ]


class HourStrip extends Card [ height = 196,
    label = "HOURLY FORECAST",
    summary: string = "",
    summaryText: Text [ x = 16, y = 32, width = { parent.width - 32 }, fontSize = 15,
        textColor = white, text = { classroot.summary } ],
    rule: View [ x = 16, y = 74, width = { parent.width - 32 }, height = 1, fill = #FFFFFF33 ],

    // `scrolls = x` makes this pane scroll horizontally INSIDE the page's
    // vertical scroll; the platform arbitrates which gesture goes where.
    // `datapath = :hours[]` replicates one HourCol per record in the city's
    // hours array; `key` names the field that identifies a record across
    // updates, so columns keep their identity when the city changes.

    scroller: View [ x = 8, y = 88, width = { parent.width - 16 }, height = 100, scrolls = x,
        row: View [ layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 4 ],
            HourCol [ datapath = :hours[], key = :t ]
            ]
        ]
    ]


// ── the 10-day forecast ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// One row per day. The range bar needs the WHOLE ten days' min and max so the
// bars are comparable — those arrive from the card, through each row, into
// the drawn bar.

class DayRow extends View [ height = 42,
    lo10: number = 0,
    hi10: number = 0,
    todayTemp: number = -1000,
    name: Text [ x = 0, y = center, width = 74, fontSize = 17, fontWeight = medium,
        textColor = white, wrap = false, text = :day ],
    icon: WIcon [ x = 78, y = center, width = 26, height = 26, kind = { "" + :icon } ],
    lo: Text [ x = 116, y = center, width = 46, fontSize = 17, fontWeight = medium,
        textColor = #FFFFFFB0, textAlign = right, wrap = false, text = { fmtTemp(:lo) } ],
    bar: RangeBar [ x = 172, y = center, height = 5,
        width = { parent.width - 172 - 54 },
        lo = { :lo }, hi = { :hi },
        min = { parent.lo10 }, max = { parent.hi10 },
        now = { :day == "Today" ? parent.todayTemp : -1000 } ],
    hi: Text [ x = { parent.width - 48 }, y = center, width = 48, fontSize = 17,
        fontWeight = medium, textColor = white, textAlign = right, wrap = false,
        text = { fmtTemp(:hi) } ],
    rule: View [ x = 0, y = { parent.height - 1 }, width = 100%, height = 1, fill = #FFFFFF22 ]
    ]


class TenDay extends Card [
    label = "10-DAY FORECAST",
    lo10: number = 0,
    hi10: number = 0,
    todayTemp: number = 0,

    // this card's height is its own arithmetic — caption + ten rows + air —
    // so it opts out of grid stretching by never declaring `baseH`

    height = { 36 + 42 * 10 + 8 },
    list: View [ x = 16, y = 34, width = { parent.width - 32 },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 0 ],
        DayRow [ width = { parent.width },
            lo10 = { classroot.lo10 }, hi10 = { classroot.hi10 },
            todayTemp = { classroot.todayTemp },
            datapath = :days[], key = :day ]
        ]
    ]


// ── the small instrument cards ─────────────────────────────────────────────
// Each pairs text with a drawn instrument from weather-art. A shared shape:
// the top block stays put, the instrument centres in whatever height the
// grid gives the card, and the caption rides the card's FOOT — so a card the
// grid stretches (to level its column) still reads as designed.

class UVCard extends Card [ label = "UV INDEX",

    note: string = "",
    big: Text [ x = 14, y = 34, fontSize = 34, fontWeight = medium, textColor = white,

    ]

// The moon card has two arrangements — a wide row-card and a small square —
// selected by `wide`. Same disc, same drawn terminator either way; only the
// arrangement differs.

class MoonCard extends Card [
    phase: string = "",
    illum: number = 0,
    moonset: string = "",
    nextFull: number = 0,
    waning: boolean = true,
    wide: boolean = true,
    label = { classroot.phase != "" ? classroot.phase.toUpperCase() : "MOON" },

        illumLabel: Text [ x = 16, y = 46, fontSize = 15, textColor = white, wrap = false, text = "Illumination" ],
        illumVal: Text [ x = 16, y = 46, width = { parent.width - 168 }, fontSize = 15, textAlign = right,
            fontWeight = medium, textColor = white, wrap = false,
            text = { "" + classroot.illum + "%" } ],
        rule1: View [ x = 16, y = 74, width = { parent.width - 168 }, height = 1, fill = #FFFFFF22 ],
        setLabel: Text [ x = 16, y = 86, fontSize = 15, textColor = white, wrap = false, text = "Moonset" ],
        setVal: Text [ x = 16, y = 86, width = { parent.width - 168 }, fontSize = 15, textAlign = right,
            fontWeight = medium, textColor = white, wrap = false, text = { classroot.moonset } ],

        fullVal: Text [ x = 16, y = 126, width = { parent.width - 168 }, fontSize = 15, textAlign = right,
            fontWeight = medium, textColor = white, wrap = false,
            text = { "" + classroot.nextFull + " DAYS" } ]
        ],

    square: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, visible = { !classroot.wide },

        // equal air above and below: the disc centres in the band between
        // the caption row and the foot caption

        disc: MoonDisc [ x = center, width = 100, height = 100,
            y = { 34 + (parent.height - 34 - 34 - 100) / 2 },
            illum = { classroot.illum / 100 }, waning = { classroot.waning } ],
        caption: Text [ x = 14, y = { parent.height - 28 }, width = { parent.width - 28 },
            fontSize = 14, textColor = #FFFFFFCC, wrap = false,
            text = { "Moonset: " + classroot.moonset } ]
        ]
    ]


// The plain value-plus-sentence card — feels like, humidity, visibility.
// One class, several uses; only the bound values differ.

class StatCard extends Card [
    value: string = "",
    sub: string = "",
    note: string = "",
    big: Text [ x = 14, y = 34, fontSize = 34, fontWeight = medium, textColor = white,
        wrap = false, text = { classroot.value } ],
    subLine: Text [ x = 14, y = 76, fontSize = 18, fontWeight = semibold, textColor = white,
        wrap = false, visible = { classroot.sub != "" }, text = { classroot.sub } ],
    noteLine: Text [ x = 14, y = { parent.height - 64 }, width = { parent.width - 28 }, fontSize = 14,
        textColor = #FFFFFFCC, text = { classroot.note } ]
    ]


class AvgCard extends Card [ label = "AVERAGES",
    delta: string = "",
    sign: string = "",
    today: number = 0,
    avg: number = 0,
    big: Text [ x = 14, y = 34, fontSize = 34, fontWeight = medium, textColor = white,
        wrap = false, text = { classroot.delta } ],
    signLine: Text [ x = 14, y = 76, width = { parent.width - 28 }, fontSize = 16,
        fontWeight = semibold, textColor = white, text = { classroot.sign } ],
    todayLabel: Text [ x = 14, y = { parent.height - 50 }, fontSize = 14, textColor = #FFFFFFA8,
        wrap = false, text = "Today" ],
    todayVal: Text [ x = 14, y = { parent.height - 50 }, width = { parent.width - 28 }, fontSize = 14,
        textAlign = right, fontWeight = semibold, textColor = white, wrap = false,
        text = { "H:" + fmtTemp(classroot.today) } ],
    avgLabel: Text [ x = 14, y = { parent.height - 28 }, fontSize = 14, textColor = #FFFFFFA8,
        wrap = false, text = "Average" ],
    avgVal: Text [ x = 14, y = { parent.height - 28 }, width = { parent.width - 28 }, fontSize = 14,
        textAlign = right, fontWeight = semibold, textColor = white, wrap = false,
        text = { "H:" + fmtTemp(classroot.avg) } ]
    ]


class MapCard extends Card [ label = "PRECIPITATION",
    base: string = "",
    amount: number = 0,
    seed: number = 7,
    pin: string = "",

    // where this city sits on its own base map, as a fraction of the plate

    px: number = 0.5,
    py: number = 0.5,
    plate: View [ x = 12, y = 32, width = { parent.width - 24 }, height = { parent.height - 44 },
        cornerRadius = 12, clip = true, fill = #EEF3F8,

        // `contain`, not `cover`: a map that has been cropped is a wrong map

        img: Image [ width = 100%, height = 100%, stretches = contain,
            source = { classroot.base } ],
        radar: RadarBlobs [ width = 100%, height = 100%,
            amount = { classroot.amount }, seed = { classroot.seed } ],
        marker: MapPin [ width = 40, height = 40, label = { classroot.pin },
            x = { parent.width * classroot.px - 20 },
            y = { parent.height * classroot.py - 20 } ]
        ]
    ]


class AQICard extends Card [ label = "AIR QUALITY",
    value: number = 0,
    note: string = "",
    line: AQILine [ x = 14, y = 32, width = { parent.width - 28 }, height = 10,
        value = { classroot.value } ],
    noteLine: Text [ x = 14, y = 50, width = { parent.width - 28 }, fontSize = 15, textColor = white,
        text = { classroot.note } ]
    ]


class AlertCard extends Card [ label = "WEATHER ALERT",
    fill = #FFFFFF26,
    body: string = "",
    bodyText: Text [ x = 14, y = 34, width = { parent.width - 28 }, fontSize = 15, textColor = white,
        text = { classroot.body } ]
    ]


// ── the card grid ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// The whole card vocabulary for ONE city. Both dialects instantiate this;
// only the width and the column count differ (2 columns on a phone, 3 or 4
// on a desktop). Every card binds its values from `city` — the guards keep
// the grid quiet before the data arrives.

class CityCards extends View [
    city: object = null,
    cols: number = 1,
    gap: number = 12,

    // one column's width, and the one place a span becomes pixels

    colW: number = { (this.width - this.gap * (this.cols - 1)) / this.cols },
    spanW(n: number) {
        const k = Math.max(1, Math.min(this.cols, n))
        return this.colW * k + this.gap * (k - 1)
        },

    // this component is exactly as tall as its packed grid

    height = { this.stack.height },

    stack: View [ width = 100%,
        layout: MasonryLayout [ cols = { classroot.cols }, gap = { classroot.gap } ],
        alert: AlertCard [ span = { classroot.cols }, width = { classroot.spanW(classroot.cols) }, height = 108,
            visible = { classroot.city != null && classroot.city.alert != "" },
            body = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.alert } ],
        hourly: HourStrip [ span = { classroot.cols }, width = { classroot.spanW(classroot.cols) },
            summary = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.summary },
            datapath = { classroot.city } ],
        tenDay: TenDay [ span = 2, width = { classroot.spanW(2) },
            lo10 = { classroot.city == null ? 0 : Math.min(...classroot.city.days.map((d) => d.lo)) },
            hi10 = { classroot.city == null ? 1 : Math.max(...classroot.city.days.map((d) => d.hi)) },
            todayTemp = { classroot.city == null ? 0 : classroot.city.temp },
            datapath = { classroot.city } ],
        map: MapCard [ span = 2, width = { classroot.spanW(2) }, baseH = 300,
            base = { classroot.city == null ? "" : "maps/" + classroot.city.map },
            amount = { classroot.city == null ? 0 : classroot.city.precipIn },
            seed = { classroot.city == null ? 7 : classroot.city.name.length * 37 + classroot.city.hi },
            pin = { classroot.city == null ? "" : fmtTemp(classroot.city.temp) },
            px = { classroot.city == null ? 0.5 : classroot.city.px },
            py = { classroot.city == null ? 0.5 : classroot.city.py } ],
        aqi: AQICard [ span = 2, width = { classroot.spanW(2) }, baseH = 96,
            value = { classroot.city == null ? 0 : classroot.city.aqi },
            note = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.aqiNote } ],
        uv: UVCard [ span = 1, width = { classroot.spanW(1) }, baseH = { SMALL_CARD_H },
            value = { classroot.city == null ? 0 : classroot.city.uv },
            name = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.uvName },
            note = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.uvNote } ],
        sunset: SunsetCard [ span = 1, width = { classroot.spanW(1) }, baseH = { SMALL_CARD_H },
            at = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.sunset },
            rise = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.sunrise },
            frac = { classroot.city == null ? 0.5 : classroot.city.dayFrac } ],
        wind: WindCard [ span = 1, width = { classroot.spanW(1) }, baseH = { SMALL_CARD_H },
            mph = { classroot.city == null ? 0 : classroot.city.windMph },
            deg = { classroot.city == null ? 0 : classroot.city.windDir },
            gusts = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.gusts } ],
        feels: StatCard [ span = 1, width = { classroot.spanW(1) }, baseH = { SMALL_CARD_H },
            label = "FEELS LIKE",
            value = { classroot.city == null ? "" : fmtTemp(classroot.city.feels) },
            note = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.feelsNote } ],
        humidity: StatCard [ span = 1, width = { classroot.spanW(1) }, baseH = { SMALL_CARD_H },
            label = "HUMIDITY",
            value = { classroot.city == null ? "" : "" + classroot.city.humidity + "%" },
            note = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.dewNote } ],
        visibility: StatCard [ span = 1, width = { classroot.spanW(1) }, baseH = { SMALL_CARD_H },
            label = "VISIBILITY",
            value = { classroot.city == null ? "" : "" + classroot.city.visMi + " mi" },
            note = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.visNote } ],
        pressure: PressureCard [ span = 1, width = { classroot.spanW(1) }, baseH = { SMALL_CARD_H },
            inHg = { classroot.city == null ? 0 : classroot.city.pressure },
            frac = { classroot.city == null ? 0.5 : classroot.city.pressureFrac } ],
        moon: MoonCard [ span = 2, width = { classroot.spanW(2) }, baseH = { SMALL_CARD_H },
            wide = true,
            waning = { classroot.city == null ? true : classroot.city.moon.includes("Waning") },
            phase = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.moon },
            illum = { classroot.city == null ? 0 : classroot.city.moonIllum },
            moonset = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.moonset },
            nextFull = { classroot.city == null ? 0 : classroot.city.nextFull } ],
        avg: AvgCard [ span = 1, width = { classroot.spanW(1) }, baseH = { SMALL_CARD_H },
            delta = { classroot.city == null ? "" : classroot.city.avgDelta },

at `open = 1` its own `y` cancels the page scroll exactly.

        swipeTo = 0
        // spring the swipe home rather than zeroing it — a close mid-swipe
        // must not jump sideways. start() also wakes the spring when its
        // target has not changed.
        swipeSpring.start()
        },

    // ── paging between cities ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    // `swipeX` is the sideways offset of the current page. While a finger is
    // down it follows the finger (the spring's target IS swipeX, so the
    // spring holds still); on release the target becomes `swipeTo` (home)
    // and the spring carries it there. The arriving neighbour rides one
    // screen-width beside it — see `peek` in the tree below.

    swipeX: number = 0,
    swipeTo: number = 0,
    dragging: boolean = false,
    dragStartX: number = 0,
    dragStartSwipe: number = 0,
    swipeSpring: Spring [ attribute = swipeX,
        to = { app.dragging ? app.swipeX : app.swipeTo },
        stiffness = { slowK(260) }, damping = { slowC(30) }, epsilon = { slowEps(0.4) } ],

    // A peek page exists only while the city view is up and the pager is
    // actually displaced — gating on `cityUp` makes a page stranded over the
    // list unrepresentable, whatever the swipe values are.

    swiping: boolean = { app.cityUp && Math.abs(app.swipeX) > 0.5 && app.peekCity != null },
    peekIndex: number = { app.swipeX < 0 ? app.cityIndex + 1 : app.cityIndex - 1 },

    // no neighbour past the ends of the list — `null`, not a clamp: clamping
    // would put the CURRENT city on both pages and show it arriving beside
    // itself

    peekSlide: number = { app.swipeX + (app.swipeX < 0 ? app.hostWidth : -app.hostWidth) },
    peekCity: object = { app.peekIndex < 0 || app.peekIndex >= app.cities.length
        ? null : app.cities[app.peekIndex] },

    // The end stops. Nothing lies beyond the first and last city, so a drag
    // that pulls that way meets resistance instead of tracking the finger:
    // the pull is compressed toward an asymptote of half a screen, which
    // reads as the list being held rather than the app being unresponsive.

    resist(raw: number) {
        const past = (raw > 0 && app.cityIndex == 0)
            || (raw < 0 && app.cityIndex >= app.cities.length - 1)
        if (!past) return raw
        const limit = app.hostWidth / 2
        const d = Math.abs(raw)
        return (raw < 0 ? -1 : 1) * d * limit / (d + limit)
        },

    // Land on a city, from either the chevrons or a completed swipe: commit
    // the index and read its page from the top. The header condenses with
    // the scroll and then rides off with it, so arriving at a page already
    // scrolled deep would leave a city with its name nowhere on screen.

    pageTo(i: number) {
        cityIndex = i
        openId = app.cities[i].id
        // the arriving city reads from its own top — the page is the document
        // now, and the city's top IS the document's top once open has landed
        app.scrollTo(0)
        },

    endSwipe(canceled: boolean) {
        if (!app.dragging) return
        dragging = false
        swipeTo = 0
        if (canceled) return
        const moved = app.swipeX
        const n = app.cities.length
        // past a third of the screen the page turns — and swipeX is REBASED
        // by a screen-width, so the new current page carries on from exactly
        // where the arriving one was, with no jump to hide
        if (moved < -app.hostWidth / 3 && app.cityIndex < n - 1) {
            pageTo(app.cityIndex + 1)
            swipeX = app.swipeX + app.hostWidth
        } else if (moved > app.hostWidth / 3 && app.cityIndex > 0) {
            pageTo(app.cityIndex - 1)
            swipeX = app.swipeX - app.hostWidth
        }
        },

    stepCity(dir: number) {
        const i = app.cityIndex + dir
        if (i < 0 || i >= app.cities.length) return
        pageTo(i)
        // synthesize the state a completed swipe rebases into — the new page
        // a screen-width out, springing home — so a tap on the chevron reads
        // as exactly the motion a swipe does. RELATIVE, exactly as the rebase
        // above is: a second tap while the first is still travelling must
        // carry on from where the pages ARE, not restage them from scratch.
        // start() wakes the spring: its target (0) has not changed, only the
        // value was displaced.
        swipeX = app.swipeX + (dir > 0 ? app.hostWidth : -app.hostWidth)
        swipeTo = 0
        swipeSpring.start()
        },

    // ── the shared clock ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // Every row's local time is the SAME instant read through its own
    // offset: one fact, twenty-five readings of it. A Time at `minute` is the
    // instrument: the readouts show minutes, so the minute turning is the only
    // moment anything changes, and the alarm is aligned to it — right at the
    // flip, and no frame loop held open to watch a wall clock (the runtime's
    // idle-zero invariant is a property worth keeping).

    clock: Time [ tick = minute ],

    // ── the dialect switch ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // One number decides which app this is; `cols` is how many small cards
    // sit side by side in the grid.

    phone: boolean = { app.hostWidth < 700 },
    cols: number = { app.hostWidth < 700 ? 2 : app.hostWidth < 1150 ? 3 : 4 },

    // ── the page shape ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // On a phone the app IS the document: its height is the arrangement's,
    // and the window is the scroller (an App scrolls vertically by default —
    // the page itself is its scroller). A browser only tucks its own bars
    // away when the PAGE scrolls, which is the whole reason a city is a row
    // here rather than an overlay with a scroller inside it. On a desktop the
    // content fits one screen and the inner panes scroll instead.
    //
    // The two extents are DECLARED rather than measured. A height that
    // measured the live rows would shrink under the scroll offset mid-
    // transition, and the browser would clamp the page out from under the
    // morph. Declared, the page only ever grows on the way open.

    rowCount: number = { app.shown.value == null ? 0 : app.shown.value.rows.length },
    cardsH: number = { app.phoneUI.city.cardsH },
    listH: number = { LIST_TOP + app.safeTop + app.rowCount * (ROW_H + ROW_GAP)
        + LIST_TAIL + app.safeBottom },
    cityH: number = { app.openAnchor + HERO_H + app.safeTop + app.cardsH
        + LIST_TAIL + app.safeBottom },

    // ...and while it is MOVING, the page holds the larger of the two extents
    // rather than interpolating: a document whose scroll height changes every
    // frame reflows the whole page every frame. Nothing scrolls mid-transition,
    // so the exact value only has to be right at the two ends.

    height = { app.phone
        ? Math.max(app.hostHeight,
            app.listGone ? app.cityH
            : app.openT < 0.002 ? app.listH
            : Math.max(app.listH, app.cityH))
        : app.hostHeight },

    // `edges = cover` is the edge-to-edge opt-in: the app extends under the
    // device's own chrome (notch, home indicator), and `app.safeTop` /
    // `app.safeBottom` report the real insets for anything that must stay
    // reachable. On a desktop the insets read 0 and nothing moves.

    edges = cover,

    // ── the backdrop ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // What the floor of the app shows: on the phone the LIST always sits on
    // the sunny sky (each open city's view carries its own); the desktop
    // shows the selected city's. `skyTone` is that sky's top-edge color —
    // the App's `fill` wears it so the browser paints its own bands (status
    // area, collapsed toolbar) to match, and the haze below fades the same
    // tone into the clouds so flat band and textured sky never meet at a
    // hard edge.

segments.md:
## What the floor shows, and when it changes

On the phone the list always sits on the sunny sky and an opened city
carries its own — so the floor must NOT follow the tap. The expansion is
the ROW's sky growing to fill the screen, not the screen changing colour
underneath it, and a backdrop that flips on touch does the second.

It swaps at the LANDING instead, where it cannot be seen: by then the
city's own sky covers the viewport edge to edge, and on the way back
`liftOff` restores it while the city still covers everything. It has to
swap at all because `fill` IS the page's background — the colour the
browser paints in the overscroll and behind its own chrome — and that band
has to match the city you are reading.

## The floor

The backdrop the list is read against. It never scrolls: it GLUES itself
to the viewport by reading the page scroll, as an ordinary first child —
so it stays behind everything in paint order.

The height carries EDGE_SLACK for the zones a browser lets content occupy
beyond the layout viewport as its chrome comes and goes, capped at the
app's own bottom (an overflowing child would grow the document).

segments.html:
sky: WSky [ width = 100%, y = { app.scrollY },
        height = { Math.min(app.hostHeight + EDGE_SLACK, app.height - app.scrollY) },
        cond = { app.backCond } ],
    dim: View [ width = 100%, y = { app.scrollY },
        height = { Math.min(app.hostHeight + EDGE_SLACK, app.height - app.scrollY) },
        fill = #0A1422, opacity = 0.10, pointerEvents = "none" ],

    // the same tone fading into the clouds, so the flat band behind the
    // browser's chrome and the textured sky never meet at a hard edge.
    // `colorWithAlpha` takes alpha as 0…255, not 0…1.

    haze: View [ width = 100%, y = { app.scrollY }, height = 140,
        visible = { app.phone }, pointerEvents = "none",
        fill = { gradient("180deg", colorWithAlpha(app.skyTone, 255), colorWithAlpha(app.skyTone, 0)) } ],

    // ── the phone dialect ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // The list IS the app, and a city IS one of its rows, expanded in place.
    // There is no second view to hand off to and no overlay: the row you
    // tapped grows until it is the page's head, every other row collapses to
    // nothing, and the cards — one object, built once — take their height and
    // land directly beneath it. The document scrolls throughout, which is why
    // the browser's own chrome behaves.

    phoneUI: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, visible = { app.phone },

        // the list's CHROME recedes as a city takes over; the rows themselves
        // do not, because one of them is becoming the city

        list: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%,
            find: TextInput [ x = center, y = { 14 + app.safeTop }, width = { parent.width - 32 },
                height = 36, cornerRadius = 18, fill = #FFFFFF1A, padding = 14,
                fontSize = 16, textColor = white, placeholder = "Search",
                opacity = { fadeOut(app.openT, 2.2) },
                visible = { app.openT < 0.45 },

                // the field owns its text and delivers it up; a constraint
                // on `text` would re-assert the old value every keystroke

                onInput() { app.query = this.text },
                onKeyDown(e: KeyEvent) {
                    if (e.key == "Escape") { this.text = ""; app.query = "" }
                    },
                clear: ClearButton [ x = { parent.width - 40 }, y = center,
                    visible = { app.query != "" },
                    onClick() { parent.text = ""; app.query = "" }
                    ]
                ],

            // a search that matches nothing says so — an empty sky is a
            // beautiful way to look broken. It centres in the SCREEN, not in
            // the list: with no rows there is nothing to sit under.

            none: Text [ x = center, y = { (app.hostHeight - this.height) / 2 },
                width = { parent.width - 64 }, textAlign = center,
                fontSize = 17, textColor = #FFFFFFC4,
                visible = { app.noMatch },
                text = "No locations match" ],

            // The rows. Each one places itself from its rank (see CityRow), so
            // this is a container rather than an arrangement — which is what
            // lets a row ride the expansion instead of being told where to be.
            // The whole list leaves in one flip when the city lands.

            rows: View [ x = center, y = { LIST_TOP + app.safeTop },
                width = { parent.width - 32 },
                visible = { !app.listGone },
                datapath = { app.listRows },
                CityRow [ datapath = :rows[], key = :id ]
                ],
            tail: View [ y = { app.listGone ? app.cityH : app.listH }, width = 100%,
                height = { LIST_TAIL + app.safeBottom } ]
            ],

        // THE ONE EXPANDED CITY — the sky, the header and the cards, in a
        // single instance. It sits beside the list rather than inside it, so
        // nothing about where it goes has to agree with the stack's spacing;
        // `cityY` carries it from the tapped row's seat to the anchor, and
        // `swipeX` slides it sideways as you page.

        city: CityView [ y = { app.cityY }, city = { app.city },
            openIn = { app.openT }, seat = { app.openSeat },
            x = { lerp(16, 0, app.openT) + app.swipeX },
            visible = { app.cityUp } ],

        // The arriving neighbour: the SAME class, bound to one record and held
        // outside the document (`ignoreScroll`), because the page's extent
        // must be exactly the city you are reading — a neighbour occupying a
        // row would add its height to the scroll range. `pinned` tells its sky
        // not to cancel a page scroll it does not ride.

        peek: CityView [ ignoreScroll = true, visible = { app.swiping },
            pinned = true, openIn = 1, city = { app.peekCity },
            x = { app.peekSlide }, y = 0 ],

        // The floating chrome: the pager pill and the back-to-list button.
        // Both clear the two bands at the foot of the screen a finger cannot
        // rely on — the home indicator's, and the browser's own, which is 0
        // while its bars are shown and their height once they retract (a tap
        // there brings the bars back instead of reaching the app). Reading
        // the live fact rather than guessing a constant is what keeps these
        // controls in ONE place on screen as the bars come and go.

        pill: GlassChip [ ignoreScroll = true,
            y = { app.hostHeight - 60 - Math.max(app.safeBottom, app.underlapBottom) },
            height = 48, cornerRadius = 24,
            x = 16, width = { parent.width - 16 - 48 - 10 - 16 },
            visible = { app.cityUp },
            opacity = { fadeIn(app.openT, 0.55, 2.2) },

            // the chevrons draw small and hit large: the glyph is the same
            // five-pixel stroke it always was, inside 44 points of target

            prev: Chevron [ x = 2, y = center, width = 44, height = 44, back = true,
                dim = { app.cityIndex <= 0 },
                onClick() { app.stepCity(-1) }
                ],
            next: Chevron [ x = { parent.width - 46 }, y = center, width = 44, height = 44,
                dim = { app.cityIndex >= app.cities.length - 1 },
                onClick() { app.stepCity(1) }
                ],

            // the dots DIVIDE the room between the chevrons, so any count
            // fills the same track

            track: View [ x = center, y = center, height = 44,
                width = { parent.width - 100 },
                dots: View [ width = 100%, height = 44,
                    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 0 ],
                    datapath = { app.pageset.value },
                    Dot [ width = { Math.max(6, parent.width / Math.max(1, app.cities.length)) },
                        datapath = :cities[], key = :id ]
                    ]
                ]
            ],
        back: GlassChip [ ignoreScroll = true,
            x = { parent.width - 64 },
            y = { app.hostHeight - 60 - Math.max(app.safeBottom, app.underlapBottom) },
            width = 48, height = 48, cornerRadius = 24, cursor = "pointer",
            visible = { app.cityUp },
            opacity = { fadeIn(app.openT, 0.55, 2.2) },
            ic: ListIcon [ x = center, y = center, width = 26, height = 26 ],
            onClick() { app.closeCity() }
            ]
        ],

    // ── the desktop dialect ───────────────────────────────────────────────

    deskUI: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, visible = { !app.phone },

        // SIDEBAR wide enough that a row's condition and its H/L do not meet
        // in the middle — the row is the phone's row, and it was designed at
        // the width of a phone

        side: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = { SIDEBAR_W }, height = 100%, scrolls = y,
            fill = #0A1422B8, backdrop = { frost(30, 1.2) },

            // the FIELD is the pill: no wrapper view to sit over the native
            // input and take its clicks

            find: TextInput [ x = 16, y = 16, width = { parent.width - 32 }, height = 36,
                cornerRadius = 18, fill = #FFFFFF1A, padding = 14,
                fontSize = 16, textColor = white, placeholder = "Search",
                onInput() { app.query = this.text },
                onKeyDown(e: KeyEvent) {
                    if (e.key == "Escape") { this.text = ""; app.query = "" }
                    },
                clear: ClearButton [ x = { parent.width - 40 }, y = center,
                    visible = { app.query != "" },
                    onClick() { parent.text = ""; app.query = "" }
                    ]
                ],
            none: Text [ x = center, y = { (parent.height - this.height) / 2 },
                width = { parent.width - 32 }, textAlign = center,
                fontSize = 16, textColor = #FFFFFFC4,
                visible = { app.noMatch },
                text = "No locations match" ],
            list: View [ x = 16, y = 64, width = { parent.width - 32 },
                datapath = { app.sideRows },
                CityRow [ width = { parent.width }, datapath = :rows[], key = :id ]
                ]
            ],

        // the content column is centred and capped: past ~1000px the cards
        // stop growing, which keeps a 10-day bar readable as a chart

        content: View [ x = { SIDEBAR_W }, y = 0, width = { parent.width - SIDEBAR_W },
            height = 100%, scrolls = y,
            col: View [ x = center, width = { Math.min(1000, parent.width - 48) },
                layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 0 ],
                head: View [ width = 100%, height = 132,
                    hero: Hero [ x = 0, y = 20, width = 100%, city = { app.city } ]
                    ],

                // one record while this dialect is in use, none otherwise —
                // so a phone never builds the grid or its instruments

                cards: View [ width = 100%, datapath = { app.deskSet.value },
                    CityCards [ datapath = :on[], key = :id,
                        width = { parent.width }, cols = { app.cols }, city = { app.city } ]
                    ],
                tail: View [ width = 100%, height = 32 ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]


// ── the pager dot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Replicated over the cities; bright for the one on screen. Each dot reads
// its own record's id and compares it to the selected city's — no index
// bookkeeping, and it stays right if the list is ever reordered.

class Dot extends View [ width = 18, height = 44, cursor = "pointer",
    mine: string = { "" + :id },
    here: boolean = { app.city != null && app.city.id == this.mine },

    // the mark shrinks with its slot, so a long list stays a row of
    // separate dots

    mark: View [ x = center, y = center, width = { Math.min(8, parent.width - 2) },
        height = { this.width }, cornerRadius = { this.width / 2 },
        fill = #FFFFFF, opacity = { classroot.here ? 1 : 0.38 } ],
    onClick() {
        if (!app.phone) { app.selectById(this.mine); return }
        // a dot has no row under it to grow from, so it names the seat the
        // row WOULD have had — the list is not on screen to disagree
        app.openRow(this.mine, app.seatOf(this.mine))
        }
    ]


// the search field's clear affordance — a small child of the input, so it
// takes only its own clicks and the rest of the pill still focuses the field.
// What you see is the 20px disc; what you hit is the 44 square around it,
// which is the smallest thing a finger reliably lands on.

class ClearButton extends View [ width = 44, height = 44, cursor = "pointer",
    disc: View [ x = center, y = center, width = 20, height = 20, cornerRadius = 10,
        fill = #FFFFFF42 ],
    cross: CloseIcon [ x = center, y = center, width = 10, height = 10,
        ink = #0A1422D0, weight = 2 ]
    ]


// the pill's step control — a drawn chevron, dimmed at the ends of the list

class Chevron extends View [ cursor = "pointer",
    back: boolean = false,
    dim: boolean = false,
    opacity = { this.dim ? 0.25 : 0.9 },
    draw(d: Draw) {
        const w = d.w, h = d.h
        d.strokeStyle = "#FFFFFF"
        d.lineWidth = 2
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.lineJoin = "round"
        const x = w / 2, y = h / 2, r = 5
        d.beginPath()
        if (this.back) { d.moveTo(x + r * 0.6, y - r); d.lineTo(x - r * 0.6, y); d.lineTo(x + r * 0.6, y + r) }
        else { d.moveTo(x - r * 0.6, y - r); d.lineTo(x + r * 0.6, y); d.lineTo(x - r * 0.6, y + r) }
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]
